text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Parents of pupils at primary and secondary schools are confused about the new eight-year compulsory education plan and how it will be implemented.
MILLIYET
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz told dissidents in his party opposing the eight-year education plan to either support the measure or the party would withdraw from power.
- The minister for the economy caused panic in the markets with a statement that inflation would be around 100 percent by year-end rather than the expected 80-85 percent.
HURRIYET
- Yilmaz ordered police accused of killing leftist journalist Metin Goktepe to attend the trial.
- Minister of transport Necdet Menzir says the first shares of Turk Telecom will be issued by the end of this year.
YENI YUZYIL
- Two deputies from the previous Islamist-led government resign from their parties in a further blow to the opposition.
- The names of 12 Turkish citizens are on the list of almost 2,000 dormant Holocaust-era Swiss bank accounts.
RADIKAL
- The Fiat group and Turkish partners Koc Holding are preparing to invest $262 million to develop a factory producing parts for Fiat cars in the western town of Bursa.
CUMHURIYET
- Foreign minister Ismail Cem says European Union membership and Cyprus should not be debated together.
DUNYA
- Businessmen are interested in investing in the southeastern province of Gaziantep after a huge dam project has brought more prosperity to the area.
ZAMAN
- Yilmaz's statement that all intelligence gathering units would be merged under the Turkish Intelligence Service received a harsh reaction from the police.
